newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Brent dips, but seen supported by weather.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Brent dips, but seen supported by weather.

text.p: Brent February crude futures were traded slightly lower in Asia on Tuesday, but brokers said they expected buying into the dip.
February Brent trading on SIMEX was traded at $24.50 per barrel, down six cents from London's settlement on Monday and following the trend of a small retracement of overnight gains on NYMEX.

However, brokers said the Arctic cold snap in Europe and the below average temperatures seen for the U.S. northeast was solidly underpinning the market and five-year highs on Brent and NYMEX remained the target.
"It just feels well bid. If you consider inventories are very low and if this weather goes on for any period of time, then prices are going much higher," one broker said.

NYMEX February crude, trading on the after-hours ACCESS system, was last traded at $26.24, down 13 cents from New York where the price rose 78 cents to $26.37. Front-month NYMEX crude hit a post Gulf conflict high of $26.80 on December 19.
The Brent high of $25.06 was struck on October 15.
Heating oil stayed firm, gaining 0.05 cent to the overnight 2.35 cents to stand on ACCESS at 73.69 cents per gallon late afternoon. --Singapore Newsroom (+65 870 3081)
